The success edge (at_exit & holding_box) -> u2 with reward 1.0 exactly captures 'reach the exit with the box in your hands', and the explicit u0->u1 fall edge plus u1->u0 pickup edge (detected via the persistent holding_box becoming true, the correct predicate for a pickup since no pickup event exists) structurally enforces 'every time the box falls, pick it up again': the terminal reward is reachable only from u0, so every box_fell must be followed by a pickup before the exit. Irrelevant propositions (siren_ringing, switch_toggled) and all other combinations are absorbed by per-state else self-loops, so siren setups and same-step co-occurrences (e.g., a toggle on a fall step) cannot derail the tracking; box_fell/at_exit/holding_box co-occurrence constraints are respected by the disjoint, mutually exclusive transition guards, and the function is total in every state. The 0.1 pickup progress reward is dense but safe and bounded: only box_fell events re-enter u1, there are at most two falls per episode, and voluntary drop/pickup cycles in u0 yield nothing, so progress reward is capped at 0.2 against a 1.0 terminal reward with no idling reward. All three states are reachable (the first fall always occurs by step 8, long before the ~10-step minimum path to the exit) and u2 is declared in FINAL_STATES and is accepting for the task. The persistent/event distinction is right (box_fell as an instantaneous event, holding_box and at_exit as persistent conditions, no invented predicates). Format matches the paper layout: nonempty FINAL_STATES header, INITIAL_STATE declared, transitions as (state, formula) -> state and rewards as (state, formula, state) -> value with every reward entry matching a declared transition. One harmless note: (u1, at_exit & holding_box) -> u2 is effectively unreachable, since entering the exit ends the episode and a pickup cannot coincide with the exit step, but it is semantically correct as a defensive success edge and does not affect safety.

def siren_ringing(env): return env.siren_ringing
def switch_toggled(env): return "toggle" in env.events_this_step
def holding_box(env): return env.carrying is not None and env.carrying.type == "box"
def box_fell(env): return "fall" in env.events_this_step
def at_exit(env): return env.grid.get(*env.agent_pos) is not None and env.grid.get(*env.agent_pos).type == "goal"

Each matches the documented truth conditions verbatim: siren_ringing reads env.siren_ringing (persistent condition); switch_toggled and box_fell read the documented event API via "toggle"/"fall" in env.events_this_step (event semantics, current-step only); holding_box checks env.carrying is not None and env.carrying.type == "box" (persistent, with a None guard before attribute access); at_exit checks the goal cell with the required 'cell is not None' guard before reading .type. All expressions return booleans, are syntactically valid Python, contain no imports, actions, or side effects, and do not mutate env or episode memory. No runtime or semantic errors: attribute accesses are guarded, env.agent_pos unpacks correctly into grid.get, and only documented API members are used. Propositions align with the reward machine's needs (box_fell, at_exit & holding_box, holding_box & !at_exit).
